facts.fact_text: The demonstration was held as planned on 14 May 2002 at around 15.00 on Freedom Square in Yerevan.
The applicant participated in the demonstration on 14 May 2002 on Freedom Square in Yerevan.
On 14 May 2002 at 23.10, the applicant was arrested.
After being arrested on 14 May 2002, the applicant was brought to the Arabkir District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի Արաբկիրի բաժին).

Police officers prepared a record of an administrative offence (վարչական իրավախախտման արձանագրություն) stating that the applicant had "organised an unlawful procession and violated the prescribed rules for holding demonstrations and street processions".

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant, in violation of the prescribed rules for holding street processions and demonstrations, on 14 May 2002 at around 16.00, participated with a group of people in an unauthorised procession.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant's participation in the unauthorised procession constituted an offence envisaged by Article 180.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք).

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it necessary, taking into consideration the circumstances of the case and the personality of the applicant, to impose an administrative penalty in the form of a fine.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan imposed a fine on the applicant in the amount of 500 Armenian drams (AMD), which was approximately EUR 1 at the material time.

Article 180.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provides that violation of the prescribed rules for organising or holding assemblies, rallies, street processions and demonstrations shall be punishable by imposition of a penalty in the amount of fifty to one hundred per cent of the fixed minimum wage.

Article 180.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provides that in exceptional cases, where in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the offender's personality the application of a financial penalty would be deemed insufficient, the violation may be punishable by imposition of administrative detention not exceeding fifteen days.

The Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR on "Rules for Organising and Holding of Assemblies, Rallies, Street Processions and Demonstrations in the USSR" of 28 July 1988 defined the requirement of prior authorisation for holding mass events.

The Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 28 July 1988 defined the authority deciding on requests for authorisation as the executive committee of the relevant local council of people's deputies.
The Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 28 July 1988 defined the procedure for making a request for authorisation and its required content.
The Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 28 July 1988 defined the decision to be taken following the examination of a request for authorisation.
The Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 28 July 1988 provided for a possibility to appeal a decision on a request for authorisation to a superior authority.

The Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 28 July 1988 set out requirements to be met when holding a mass event, including that the event must take place at the time and place specified in the request, that public order must be respected, and that no carrying of arms was permitted.
The Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 28 July 1988 defined the reasons for refusal of an authorisation for a mass event.

The Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 28 July 1988 defined the grounds on which a particular mass event could be dispersed, including absence of a request, refusal of an authorisation, and violation of public order.
On 28 April 2004, the Armenian Parliament adopted a law regulating the procedure for holding assemblies, rallies, street processions and demonstrations.

Article 16 of the Law on Holding Assemblies, Rallies, Street Processions and Demonstrations of 28 April 2004 stated that, from the date of its entry into force, the Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR on "Rules for Organising and Holding of Assemblies, Rallies, Street Processions and Demonstrations in the USSR" of 28 July 1988 was not to be applied on the territory of the Republic of Armenia.
